description:
An agentic IDE that helps you do your best work with features such as specs, steering, and hooks.

Kiro is an agentic IDE that helps you go from prototype to production with spec-driven development. From simple to complex tasks, Kiro works alongside you to turn prompts into detailed specs, then into working code, docs, and tests—so what you build is exactly what you want and ready to share with your team. Kiro's agents help you solve challenging problems and automate tasks like generating documentation and unit tests. With Kiro, you can build beyond prototypes while being in the driver's seat every step of the way.
Memory Across Chat Sessions
This release brings Memory to every Kiro IDE user. It also makes find more reliable in long Markdown Review documents, fixes a sign-in screen that ignored Cancel, and fixes Kiro failing to start after a .deb install on Ubuntu 24.04.
Carry useful context across sessions with Memory
Memory lets Kiro carry useful context such as repository conventions, corrections, and approaches already ruled out from one session to the next. Select the Memories icon in the activity bar to open the Memory view and review what Kiro remembers. Chat shows when Kiro accesses or changes a memory. Choose how Kiro uses and learns from memories in the Kiro Agent: Memory setting, including Use only, which lets Kiro use memories without changing them. Learn more ->
